label: "n" as the first input token (plus a weak echo for "k n" at t=1)
explanation: Fires only when the input token is "n" at the very first step (t=0). It is close to binary there, at about 1.12, which is the max. It also fires very weakly (about 0.07) when "n" is the second token right after a leading "k". It never fires on "n" at later original positions, or in the delimiter or copy phases, even when n is being copied back. On the dev split, t==0 & in_tok==n alone gets F1 0.98 and mass recall 0.998; adding the k-n clause brings dev F1 to 1.0.

issues: No systematic issues found. On the test split the full predicate scores P=R=F1=mass recall=1.0 with 0 misses and 0 false positives (17294 active steps).

Checked each claim. t==0 & n alone gets test P=1.0, R=0.967, F1=0.983, mass recall 0.998. The k-n clause alone gets P=1.0 (579/579) and carries 0.24% of the mass. On dev, every leftover activation is exactly 0.07 relative at step 1 after a leading k. The feature is silent at t>=2, in the delimiter phase and in the copy phase (dev profile shows 0 active steps). It only fires on in_tok n. Magnitude: max 1.122, median 1.122, mean 1.088, which fits 'near-binary at ~1.12'.
Small wording note: the explanation gives the weak echo as about 0.07 in absolute terms. In the misses output, 0.07 is relative to the max, so the absolute value is about 0.08. This doesn't matter.
